pr_title: soc/intel_adsp: Fixups for cavs18 SMP boot
pr_body:
This platform was stale for a long time and got a little left behind.
Basic OS stuff was working but secondary core bringup didn't.  It has
a slightly different set of choices from the "weird hardware
quirks" menu:

+ Like cAVS 1.5, it boots from a ROM that needs a short delay after
  power-up before it can receive the startup IDC.

+ But, like 2.5 and unlike 1.5, it doesn't start running until the
  PWRCTL bit for the core gets set by DSP software (1.5 gets launched
  by the host).  So the delay needed to move down a bit.

+ Uniquely on this platform, the ROM likes to scribble on the
  interrupt controller and mask its own IDC interrupts after we've
  already set it up.  They have to be unmasked.  We had code to do
  this already, thinking it was a workaround for legecy SOF code (that
  we never actually located).  Now I'm thinking it was this behavior
  all along being detected by SOF's more extensive hardware CI.  Take
  out the test and do it always, it's like nine instructions.

+ The host/loader-side behavior is a mix of 1.5 and 2.5.  It won't
  actually start the secondary cores under host command, but it does
  need to see bits set for them in ADSPCS for the DSP-initiated
  power-up to work (2.5 would just ignore all but core 0's bits).

Signed-off-by: Andy Ross <andrew.j.ross@intel.com>

Fixes #42010
pr_comments: Verified #42010 issue fixed by this PR.

> longer out I'd like to see flags/configs for each workaround set by each soc as needed. That way things don't break as soon as say a cavs28 or cavs30 or whatever the future might bring is introduced and this whole section needs to be reworked

Oh, come on. :)  It's not that bad.  We have four hardware variants (though only three under active test within Zephyr) and this file has five version tests in it[1].  Hardware is cranky, and this hardware feature (MP coordination) in particular has had trouble deciding on a stable interface[2].  But this really seems pretty straightforward to me.  And do remember that future versions won't be selecting from this menu, they'll be inventing whole new quirks anyway.

[1]  The loader script has more, to be fair, but then that's not the OS and not subject to the same quality requirements.  Also python makes that kind of code a little cleaner.

[2] In no small part because the entity that should have been responsible for deciding on the interface, Cadence, basically bailed on the task and left it up to customers doing IP integration.

issue_context.title: intel_adsp_cavs18: Test cases failed on SMP related test cases (when CONFIG_MP_NUM_CPUS > 1)
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
Many test suites failed in intel_adsp_cavs18 hardware board, this issue is likely to be SMP related:

tests/kernel/smp/ (no output)
tests/kernel/spinlock/ (no output)
tests/kernel/mp/ (no output)
tests/kernel/workq/work/ (no output, but with -DCONFIG_MP_NUM_CPUS=1 only test_smp_simple_queue, test_1cpu_sync_queue, test_smp_running_cancel)

And bellow test suites failed without any output log, but they can pass with -DCONFIG_MP_NUM_CPUS=1:

tests/kernel/profiling/profiling_api/ 
tests/kernel/mem_protect/sys_sem/
tests/kernel/msgq/msgq_api/
tests/kernel/msgq/msgq_usage/ 
tests/kernel/queue/
tests/kernel/obj_tracking/ 
tests/kernel/events/event_api/ 
tests/kernel/fatal/message_capture/
tests/kernel/mbox/mbox_usage/ 
tests/kernel/threads/thread_stack/
tests/kernel/lifo/lifo_api/ 
tests/kernel/mutex/sys_mutex/ 
tests/kernel/mem_slab/mslab_concept/
tests/kernel/fifo/fifo_api/ 
tests/kernel/timer/timer_monotonic/ 
tests/kernel/mem_heap/k_heap_api/ 
tests/kernel/mem_heap/mheap_api_concept/ 
tests/kernel/condvar/condvar_api/ 
tests/kernel/semaphore/smaphore/
tests/kernel/device/

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. west build -b intel_adsp_cavs18 -p always -t tests/kernel/smp/
2. west sign -d build -t rimage -p /home/ztest/zephyrproject/modules/audio/sof/rimage/build/rimage -D /home/ztest/zephyrproject/modules/audio/sof/rimage/config -- -k /home/ztest/zephyrproject/modules/audio/sof/keys/otc_private_key.pem --no-manifest
3. ssh root@localhost "boards/xtensa/intel_adsp_cavs15/tools/cavs-fw-v15.py build/zephyr/zephyr.ri"
4. python3 -u ${ZEPHYR_BASE}/boards/xtensa/intel_adsp_cavs15/tools/adsplog.py
5. You can see there is no output from ADSP.

**Expected behavior**
There should be testing messaged output. No matter it passed or failed

**Impact**
The whole kernel test pass rate down to 50%.

**Logs and console output**
```
Firmware completing manifest v1.8
 meta: completing ADSP manifest
 meta: limit is 0x16b80
 auth: completing authentication manifest
 cse: ri_css_v1_8_hdr_create completing CSS manifest
 css: set build date to 2022:00:20

Firmware file size 0x1b000 page count 21

Firmware manifest and signing completed !
INFO:cavs-fw:cAVS firmware loader v15
INFO:cavs-fw:Mapped PCI bar 0 of length 16384 bytes.

INFO:cavs-fw:Mapped 2M huge page at 0x15a200000 to contain 86016 bytes of firmware
INFO:cavs-fw:Filled the buffer descriptor list (BDL) for DMA.
INFO:cavs-fw:ADSPCS = 0xf0f0000

(hang up and no output here .....)
```

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS:  Linux
 - Toolchain: Zephyr SDK 0.13.2
 - Commit SHA or Version used: f08c44def5fc

**Additional context**
comments: I don't have this hardware currently, so I'm going to take myself off as assignee while we find someone else to look at this.  Most likely this is a kconfig mistake or accidental regression with recent work.  The MP mechanisms here are almost the same as 1.5 and 2.5.  And IIRC SOF has 1.8 zephyr multiprocessor setups that don't seem to be failing.

Indeed, secondary core startup wasn't working (but amusingly in a way that SOF was insulated from by an existing workaround, so they never noticed).  Fix up at https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/42063 should unblock things.  I haven't done a full twister run yet though.

review_comments: this change as about cavs18, why are we removing this section related to v15?
It's being moved to below the write to PWRCTL.  It used to apply only to 1.5, now it applies to 1.5 and 1.8  (which is expressed as "not 2.5").
